## 1. Quantitative Finance / Trading / Monte Carlo Simulation

### Key Insights

- **Monte Carlo remains foundational** in 2026 for risk management (VaR, CVaR, drawdowns), derivative pricing, and strategy stress-testing
- **Critical for position sizing** — reveals how different risk allocations impact probability of ruin
- **Beyond backtesting** — Monte Carlo generates probabilistic forecasts vs. single historical sequences
- **Platforms:** QuantConnect (custom Monte Carlo logic), StrategyQuant X (up to 100K runs), Python/NumPy for custom implementations
- **Core process:** Define model → estimate parameters (drift, volatility) → generate random paths → aggregate → analyze distribution
- **2026 relevance:** Essential for preparing for extreme scenarios; accuracy depends on input quality and distribution choices

### Sources
- quantinsti.com, interactivebrokers.com, quantpedia.com, tradezella.com

## 2. AI Agents / LLMs

### Key Insights

- **Agentic AI is the paradigm shift** — from chatbots to autonomous agents executing multi-step workflows with minimal human oversight
- **Gartner prediction:** 40% of enterprise apps will incorporate task-specific AI agents by end of 2026 (vs. <5% in 2025)
- **Multi-agent systems rising** — specialized agents collaborating on complex workflows (analyze → report → trigger actions)
- **LLMs as reasoning engines** — enabling natural language understanding, planning, tool use
- **Key enablers:** Massive context windows (millions of tokens), MCP protocol, frameworks (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen)
- **Market size:** $10.91B in 2026 → $182.97B by 2033
- **Enterprise adoption:** 74% expect moderate agentic AI use within 2 years; 50% of generative AI users will deploy agents by 2027
- **Vertical/specialized agents** gaining traction — often outperform general-purpose
- **SLMs as microservices** — enterprise-ready for low latency, data privacy, cost control

### Sources
- Gartner, blueprism.com, towardsai.net, insightmarkresearch.com, medium.com
